messages:
jamie: FYI customer pasted this in support ticket — their CI scan flagged a Redwood API key in git history (public fork). They want immediate rotation + proof of deletion from our side. Link: https://github.com/example/repo/commit/abc123 :eyes:

alex: Thanks — can you paste the key id (looks like rwd_live_...)? If we have the key id we can revoke immediately. Also need to know whether it's a scoped key (org/app) or account key.

jamie: customer says the key starts with rwd_prod_7a2f and is used from their deployment pipeline (so likely org-level service key). They provided the commit hash and file path: infra/ci/secrets.yml

alex: OK. I'll revoke and create replacement. Steps I'm going to run (will post results):

```bash
# revoke existing key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/revoke 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"key_id":"rwd_prod_7a2f"}'

# issue new scoped key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/create 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"scopes":["inference:invoke"],"expires_in":86400}'
```

alex: Also will attach the audit log export for the key usage window. Expect ~2–5m.

sara: Please pause before deleting any customer logs or backups. For compliance we need to preserve the audit trail for the time window customer requests and for our internal investigation. Customer asked to "delete traces" — clarify we can revoke keys and redact from our UI but must retain audit logs for 90 days per policy.

jamie: Called customer to clarify. They confirmed they want the key rotated now and an export of auth/events for last 30 days. They understand logs must be retained for compliance.

ops-oncall: Quick checklist for eng/infra: verify whether the compromised token was wrapped by KMS/HSM or stored plaintext in our DB snapshot. If wrapped, note CMK id. If plaintext, we need to run a retrospective scan on backups and s3 snapshots.

alex: Results: revoke call returned 200, key status=revoked. Generated replacement key rwd_temp_9cde (expires in 24h). Pasted the new key to customer's secure chat and recommended rotating their pipeline env var immediately.

alex: Attaching audit export (csv) for key rwd_prod_7a2f for 2025-11-01..2026-03-01 — includes IPs and request paths. (internal note: redacted PII).

security-bot: [ticket created] sec-2026-0042 — Incident created for leaked key in customer repo. Owner: sara. Severity: medium. Required follow-ups: backup scan, KMS status, retention confirmation.

sara: Confirmed we will not erase audit logs. Action items for infra: run a targeted S3 snapshot scan for the key string pattern, enumerate any snapshots created between commit date and now, and mark any object for redaction in collaboration with record-retention. Please report counts.

ops-oncall: Kickoff done. Scan started against buckets: customer-backups-prod, infra-snapshots. ETA ~45m. Will post results.

jamie: Customer asked for a short statement they can share internally: can we provide a one-paragraph summary stating: key revoked at TIMESTAMP, replacement issued, audit export delivered, backups under scan, logs retained per policy?

alex: Draft statement (send to customer):

"We rotated and revoked the identified API key (rwd_prod_7a2f) at 2026-03-12T16:08:12Z. A replacement key with a 24-hour TTL was issued for your pipeline to minimize downtime. We provided an export of auth events for the requested window and have initiated a targeted scan of backups and snapshots for occurrences of the key. Per our retention policy, audit logs will be preserved for compliance; we cannot delete server-side audit records. If you need a longer-lived replacement key or an org-scoped token, we can issue one under your rotated credentials."

sara: OK. Add a line about recommended customer remediation: rotate any tokens in their CI, invalidate cached copies, rotate downstream secrets, and rotate any keys that were pushed to forks.

jamie: Sent to customer. They acknowledged and asked for evidence that KMS wrapping was used for their previous key.

ops-oncall: Verified: key metadata shows envelope encryption via kms://cmk-03f9. No HSM flag set on record (customer uses cloud KMS). I'll attach CMK id and link to KMS audit showing wrap/unwrap events.

sara: Good. Note for the incident: no evidence of internal exposure, only customer-side commit leak. Closing with remediation steps.

alex: Final: scan completed — found 2 additional occurrences in archived snapshot objects. Both objects are scheduled for redaction; customer notified. No active requests from those objects in last 90 days.

jamie: Customer confirmed rotation successful and pipeline green. They asked for a short write-up for their compliance team — I've attached the incident summary and audit CSV.

security-bot: [sec-2026-0042] status -> resolved by sara at 2026-03-12T18:02:00Z :white_check_mark:

jamie: Closing thread — notes: consider adding proactive repo-scan detect rule to onboarding checklist for org keys, and add a UI flag to allow customers to auto-rotate leaked pipeline keys. :bulb:
